A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acid-induced formation of molten globule states in the wild type and three different variants of E. coli 5-enoylpyruvyl shikimate 3 phosphate synthase has been demonstrated.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the wild type and its variants can acquire MG states at low pH and the stability of these states is related to the stability of the native protein.
the acid-induced formation of MG states in these EPSPS mutants is a consequence of the destabilization of the native state, rather than stabilization of the MG state.
MG state of EPSPS variants is stabilized by the mutations, and the mutations affect the stability of the folding intermediates in the same way as the stability of the folded protein.
